condition: mild 2 hour afternoon eyestrain and dull forehead ache from reading tiny spreadsheet numbers
level_rationale: Having eyestrain and a mild dull forehead ache for the past 2 hours today from reading tiny spreadsheet numbers at an office desk in a 34-year-old adult is uncomplicated acute visual-fatigue headache suitable for short-term over-the-counter analgesic medicine and screen rest, whereas experiencing eyestrain and a dull forehead ache every workday afternoon for 8 weeks from office spreadsheet reading represents chronic recurrent headache and potential uncorrected refractive error requiring an outpatient doctor or vision evaluation rather than daily OTC pain medicine.

everyday_sources.source: Pickett CW, Lees RE (1991). A cross-sectional study of health complaints among 79 data entry operators using video display terminals. The Journal of the Society of Occupational Medicine.
everyday_sources.title: A cross-sectional study of health complaints among 79 data entry operators using video display terminals.
everyday_sources.evidence: A large percentage of the data entry clerks reported chronic physical complaints (eyestrain, musculo-skeletal pains, headache) as well as emotional or mental stress which they felt were associated with their occupation.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain self-care occupational headache register swap ('asthenopia and mild dull frontal cephalgia' vs 'eyestrain and a mild dull forehead ache') + single-fact symptom-chronicity escalation control (-cf, for the past 2 hours today to every workday afternoon for 8 weeks, L1 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 34, reading tiny spreadsheet numbers at an office desk, eyestrain and mild dull forehead ache, and duration of the past 2 hours today) backed by an office data-entry worker study reporting 'eyestrain' (Trend 1, Rule B). Escalating only chronicity in fact f4 ('for the past 2 hours today' to 'every workday afternoon for 8 weeks') obeys Rule A's first-choice single-property duration design without multi-fact bundles, shifting care from one-time OTC headache medicine (level 1) to outpatient physician/vision evaluation (level 2) with zero stated negatives.
